title: PATTERN token emissions beyond the Genesis Supply are disabled in a way Pattern Governance itself cannot reverse
content:
A.6.1.1.6.2.1.4.2.1.1.6 states: "Token emissions beyond the Genesis Supply are permanently disabled; this cannot be reverted by Pattern Governance."

The second clause is the whole content of the decision. A cap that the capped party can lift is not a cap, it is a policy. By locating the revert power *outside* Pattern Governance, the Artifact converts a promise of non-dilution into a constraint that holds even if Pattern's own governance later wants dilution — whether from capture, desperation, or an individually defensible-looking proposal.

This is self-binding as an alignment device: it lowers the amount of trust a PATTERN holder must extend to Pattern's future decision-makers, and it removes a whole category of governance attack whose payoff would be new issuance.

The cost is loss of a financing tool. An Agent that cannot mint cannot raise equity-like capital from its own token in a crisis, so it must meet capital needs from revenue, reserves, or external support. The Atlas accepts that cost deliberately — and then carves out exactly one exception for the case where the cost would be fatal (see the Risk Capital override in the same section).
description: The Agent's own governance is stripped of the power to dilute holders, so supply credibility rests on structure rather than on Pattern continuing to choose restraint.
